141	def rotate_metrics(path):
142	    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.
143	
144	    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
145	    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
146	    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number
147	    back out; an empty log seals an empty segment.  Afterwards ``path``
148	    exists again as an empty file ready for appending.  Every record
149	    acknowledged by a write ends up either wholly in a segment or wholly
150	    in the current log, never split across two.
151	
152	    A crash after the rename but before the live file is recreated still
153	    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the
154	    live log.
155	
156	    Raises:
157	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
158	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
159	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, locking fails, or another OS
160	            error occurs while sealing.  Nothing is written when locking
161	            fails.
162	    """
163	    if not isinstance(path, str):
164	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
165	    if os.path.isdir(path):
166	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
167	
168	    fd = _open_locked(path, create=False)
169	    try:
170	        _finish_staged_compact(path)
171	        used = _segment_numbers(path)
172	        number = (max(used) + 1) if used else 1
173	        segment = f"{path}.{number}"
174	        # The rename atomically publishes the sealed inode under its
175	        # segment name; the lock we hold makes concurrent appenders reopen
176	        # the path before writing.
177	        os.rename(path, segment)
178	        # Re-create an empty current log.  An appender racing the rename
179	        # window may have created the path and landed a record there first;
180	        # opening without O_TRUNC keeps that record in the current log,
181	        # where it belongs.
182	        new_fd = os.open(
183	            path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
184	        )
185	        os.close(new_fd)
186	    finally:
187	        os.close(fd)
188	
189	
190	def append_metrics(path, line):
191	    """Validate one metric line and append it to the log at ``path``.
192	
193	    The line must be a string holding a JSON object whose values are ints
194	    or floats (booleans are rejected).  It is rendered canonically before
195	    writing, so every call adds exactly one compact newline-terminated
196	    record regardless of the input's spacing.
197	
198	    If another process rotates the log while this call waits for the lock,
199	    the descriptor is re-opened against the freshly re-created file before
200	    writing, so no record is directed into a sealed segment.
201	
202	    Raises:
203	        OSError: ``line`` or ``path`` is not a string, the target cannot
204	            be written, or locking the log fails.  Nothing is written when
205	            locking fails.
206	        ValueError: the line is not valid JSON, its top level is not an
207	            object, or a value is NaN or Infinity.
208	        TypeError: a metric value is neither an int nor a float.
209	    """
210	    if not isinstance(line, str):
211	        raise OSError(
212	            f"metrics line must be a string, got {type(line).__name__}"
213	        )
214	    if not isinstance(path, str):
215	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
216	    metrics = parse_metrics(line)
217	    payload = render_metrics(metrics).encode("utf-8")
218	
219	    fd = _open_locked(path, create=True)
220	    try:
221	        _finish_staged_compact(path)
222	        # One line per write loop on an O_APPEND descriptor: the kernel
223	        # appends each write atomically, so concurrent processes do not
224	        # tear or interleave records.
225	        view = memoryview(payload)
226	        while view:
227	            written = os.write(fd, view)
228	            view = view[written:]
229	    finally:
230	        os.close(fd)
231	
232	
233	def _segment_members(path):
234	    """Return the segment-set member file paths in read/write order.
235	
236	    Numbered segments come first in ascending order, followed by the
237	    current log when it exists.  The ``path.compact`` staging file is
238	    never part of this list: while present it replaces the whole list
239	    via :func:`_resolve_members`.
240	    """
241	    members = [
242	        f"{path}.{number}" for number in sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
243	    ]
244	    if os.path.exists(path):
245	        members.append(path)
246	    return members
247	
248	
249	def _resolve_members(path):
250	    """Pick the member files to read, honouring a published staging file.
251	
252	    A compaction publishes ``path.compact`` with a single atomic rename
253	    of a fully written and flushed file, so the name only ever holds a
254	    complete whole segment.  While it exists -- during cleanup or after a
255	    crash interrupted cleanup -- it alone is the segment set, and the
256	    record sequence it yields equals the pre-compaction one item by item.
257	    A crash earlier, while the merge is still being written, leaves the
258	    half-written private temp file instead; that never carries this name
259	    and so neither joins recovery nor affects reads.
260	    """
261	    staging = _staging_path(path)
262	    if os.path.exists(staging):
263	        return [staging]
264	    return _segment_members(path)
265	
266	
267	def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
268	    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.
269	
270	    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
271	    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
272	    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
273	    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
274	    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
275	    """
276	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
277	    pending = b""
278	    lineno = 0
279	    try:
280	        while True:
281	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
282	            if not chunk:
283	                break
284	            pending += chunk
285	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
286	            for raw in complete:
287	                lineno += 1
288	                yield lineno, raw
289	    finally:
290	        os.close(fd)
291	
292	
293	def _parse_file(path, label):
294	    """Stream one segment or the current log through the metrics parser."""
295	    for lineno, raw in _iter_lines(path):
296	        if not raw or raw == b"\r":
297	            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
298	            continue
299	        try:
300	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
301	            yield parse_metrics(text)
302	        except ValueError as exc:
303	            raise ValueError(
304	                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
305	            ) from exc
306	
307	
308	def iter_metrics(path):
309	    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.
310	
311	    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
312	    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
313	    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
314	    a single line may be arbitrarily long.
315	
316	    When a compaction has staged its merged segment at ``path.compact``
317	    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
318	    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
319	    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.
320	
321	    A torn unterminated tail at the end of any file is silently discarded;
322	    a segment holding only a torn tail yields nothing.  Blank empty lines
323	    (``\\n``) and CRLF blank lines (``\\r\\n``) are skipped.  Any other
324	    complete line that is not a metrics JSON object raises
325	    :class:`ValueError` naming the file and its 1-based line number.
326	
327	    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
328	    content problems are reported lazily as the offending line is reached.
329	
330	    Raises:
331	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
332	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
333	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
334	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics JSON
335	            object (raised while iterating).
336	    """
337	    if not isinstance(path, str):
338	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
339	    if os.path.isdir(path):
340	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
341	
342	    members = _resolve_members(path)
343	    if not members:
344	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")
345	
346	    def _generate():
347	        for member in members:
348	            yield from _parse_file(member, member)
349	
350	    return _generate()
351	
352	
353	def recover_metrics(path):
354	    """Read metric records back from the rotated log set at ``path``.
355	
356	    Segments are read in ascending order followed by the current log; see
357	    :func:`iter_metrics` for the line-level rules.  This materialises the
358	    records into a list, while :func:`iter_metrics` streams them.
359	
360	    Raises:
361	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
362	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
363	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics object.
364	    """
365	    return list(iter_metrics(path))
366	
367	
368	def _iter_raw_records(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
369	    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.
370	
371	    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
372	    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
373	    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
374	    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
375	    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives compaction
376	    untouched.
377	    """
378	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
379	    pending = b""
380	    try:
381	        while True:
382	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
383	            if not chunk:
384	                break
385	            pending += chunk
386	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
387	            for raw in complete:
388	                if raw and raw != b"\r":
389	                    yield raw + b"\n"
390	    finally:
391	        os.close(fd)
392	
393	
394	def _truncate_live_log(path):
395	    """Shrink the current log to zero bytes without unlinking its path.
396	
397	    Keeping the inode and path in place means a process that waits on the
398	    lock during compaction never observes -- and so never recreates -- a
399	    missing live log: once it takes the lock the path is still the same
400	    empty file.
401	    """
402	    fd = os.open(
403	        path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
404	    )
405	    os.close(fd)
406	
407	
408	def _finish_staged_compact(path):
409	    """Finish compaction cleanup when a staging file is present.
410	
411	    Called with the live-log lock held, both at the end of
412	    :func:`compact_metrics` and by any append, rotation or compaction
413	    that finds a staging file left by a crashed cleanup.  The staging
414	    file only ever holds a whole fully landed segment, so finishing is
415	    pure filesystem cleanup.
416	
417	    The staging file stays the sole authoritative member (see
418	    :func:`_resolve_members`) until the final step: old numbered
419	    segments are removed and the current log is emptied while reads
420	    still resolve to staging, and only then is staging renamed onto
421	    ``path.1``.  The rename is atomic, so a crash at any point leaves
422	    either staging alone or the finished set, and the readable record
423	    sequence equals the pre-compaction one item by item throughout.
424	    """
425	    staging = _staging_path(path)
426	    if not os.path.exists(staging):
427	        return
428	    for number in _segment_numbers(path):
429	        os.unlink(f"{path}.{number}")
430	    _truncate_live_log(path)
431	    os.replace(staging, f"{path}.1")
432	
433	
434	def compact_metrics(path):
435	    """Merge every segment and the current log into one segment.
436	
437	    All records are copied into the fixed segment ``path.1`` in write
438	    order; the current log is left empty afterwards.  Records move byte
439	    for byte with their original newlines -- nothing is re-rendered,
440	    de-duplicated or reordered, so ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key
441	    order are all preserved.  Residual torn lines are not records and
442	    are dropped; blank lines are skipped as on read; overlong single
443	    lines move as-is.  A completely empty set still produces an empty
444	    ``path.1``.
445	
446	    The merge is first written to a private temporary file and only
447	    renamed onto ``path.compact`` after the whole file has landed and
448	    been flushed, so that name always holds a complete whole segment:
449	    a half-written file left by a crash never joins recovery and never
450	    affects reads.  Once staged, recovery and streaming read only that
451	    segment; cleanup publishes it as ``path.1``, removes the other
452	    numbered segments and empties the current log.  An interrupted
453	    cleanup is finished transparently by the next append, rotation or
454	    compaction.
455

"""Durable append-only metric log with rotation, compaction and resume.

Each metric occupies exactly one newline-terminated JSON line.  A record is
appended with :func:`os.write` against a single ``O_APPEND`` file
descriptor, so concurrent appending processes never interleave one line
with another.  Recovery acknowledges only newline-terminated lines: a
record torn by a mid-write crash survives as an unterminated tail and is
silently discarded.

:func:`rotate_metrics` seals the current log into a numbered segment
(``path.1``, ``path.2``, ...) and leaves an empty log behind.  Segment
numbers are one past the highest number ever used, so deleting a segment
from the outside never makes its number come back.  Recovery walks the
segments in ascending order followed by the current log, so a record
accepted before a rotation never crosses a segment boundary.
:func:`iter_metrics` performs the same walk as a line-by-line generator,
never loading the segment set into memory.

:func:`compact_metrics` merges every segment and the current log into the
single fixed segment ``path.1`` and leaves an empty current log.  Records
are copied byte for byte, still newline terminated, without re-rendering.
The merge lands first in a staging file at ``path.compact``; only after it
is fully on disk does cleanup begin.

:func:`resume_metrics` resumes the same write-order walk at an integer
read position counting records already read from the start; the position
needs no translation across appends, rotations, compactions or crash
cleanup.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

from . import parse_metrics, render_metrics

try:  # POSIX-only; the lock guards O_APPEND and serialises rotation.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on non-POSIX platforms
    fcntl = None

__all__ = [
    "append_metrics",
    "recover_metrics",
    "rotate_metrics",
    "iter_metrics",
    "compact_metrics",
    "resume_metrics",
]

_READ_CHUNK = 1 << 20
# Suffix of the staging file compaction writes before cleanup begins; it
# only ever names a whole, fully-fsynced segment that has been published.
_COMPACT_SUFFIX = ".compact"


def _segment_numbers(path):
    """Return the already-used segment numbers for ``path`` as a set.

    The ``path.compact`` staging file is never a numbered segment and is
    deliberately invisible here.
    """
    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + "."
    numbers = set()
    try:
        names = os.listdir(directory or ".")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return numbers
    for name in names:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            suffix = name[len(prefix):]
            if suffix == "compact":
                continue
            if suffix.isascii() and suffix.isdigit():
                numbers.add(int(suffix))
    return numbers


def _staging_path(path):
    """The compaction staging file path (``path.compact``)."""
    return path + _COMPACT_SUFFIX


def _same_inode(fd, path):
    """True when ``fd`` still names the file currently found at ``path``.

    A rotation can rename the file while we wait for its lock, leaving the
    descriptor aimed at a sealed segment.  A momentarily missing ``path``
    (rotation crashed before recreating it) also reports False, so an
    appender reopens and recreates the live log.
    """
    try:
        current = os.stat(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return False
    held = os.fstat(fd)
    return (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == (held.st_dev, held.st_ino)


def _open_locked(path, create):
    """Open the current log, take the exclusive lock, and follow rotation.

    Waits for the inter-process lock and then re-checks that the
    descriptor still names the live inode: a rotation may have swapped the
    path to a fresh file while we waited.  When that happened the sealed
    descriptor is dropped and the call re-opens the new current log and
    takes its lock, so a record is never written into a segment and two
    rotations never pick the same segment number.

    ``create`` determines whether a missing log is created (append) or
    reported (rotation).  A lock failure closes the descriptor and leaves
    nothing written.
    """
    def _open():
        if create:
            return os.open(
                path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
            )
        return os.open(path, os.O_RDWR)

    fd = _open()
    if fcntl is None:
        return fd
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
    except OSError:
        os.close(fd)
        raise
    while not _same_inode(fd, path):
        os.close(fd)
        fd = _open()
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        except OSError:
            os.close(fd)
            raise
    return fd


def rotate_metrics(path):
    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.

    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number
    back out; an empty log seals an empty segment.  Afterwards ``path``
    exists again as an empty file ready for appending.  Every record
    acknowledged by a write ends up either wholly in a segment or wholly
    in the current log, never split across two.

    A crash after the rename but before the live file is recreated still
    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the
    live log.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, locking fails, or another OS
            error occurs while sealing.  Nothing is written when locking
            fails.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")

    fd = _open_locked(path, create=False)
    try:
        _finish_staged_compact(path)
        used = _segment_numbers(path)
        number = (max(used) + 1) if used else 1
        segment = f"{path}.{number}"
        # The rename atomically publishes the sealed inode under its
        # segment name; the lock we hold makes concurrent appenders reopen
        # the path before writing.
        os.rename(path, segment)
        # Re-create an empty current log.  An appender racing the rename
        # window may have created the path and landed a record there first;
        # opening without O_TRUNC keeps that record in the current log,
        # where it belongs.
        new_fd = os.open(
            path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
        )
        os.close(new_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def append_metrics(path, line):
    """Validate one metric line and append it to the log at ``path``.

    The line must be a string holding a JSON object whose values are ints
    or floats (booleans are rejected).  It is rendered canonically before
    writing, so every call adds exactly one compact newline-terminated
    record regardless of the input's spacing.

    If another process rotates the log while this call waits for the lock,
    the descriptor is re-opened against the freshly re-created file before
    writing, so no record is directed into a sealed segment.

    Raises:
        OSError: ``line`` or ``path`` is not a string, the target cannot
            be written, or locking the log fails.  Nothing is written when
            locking fails.
        ValueError: the line is not valid JSON, its top level is not an
            object, or a value is NaN or Infinity.
        TypeError: a metric value is neither an int nor a float.
    """
    if not isinstance(line, str):
        raise OSError(
            f"metrics line must be a string, got {type(line).__name__}"
        )
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
    metrics = parse_metrics(line)
    payload = render_metrics(metrics).encode("utf-8")

    fd = _open_locked(path, create=True)
    try:
        _finish_staged_compact(path)
        # One line per write loop on an O_APPEND descriptor: the kernel
        # appends each write atomically, so concurrent processes do not
        # tear or interleave records.
        view = memoryview(payload)
        while view:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
            view = view[written:]
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _segment_members(path):
    """Return the segment-set member file paths in read/write order.

    Numbered segments come first in ascending order, followed by the
    current log when it exists.  The ``path.compact`` staging file is
    never part of this list: while present it replaces the whole list
    via :func:`_resolve_members`.
    """
    members = [
        f"{path}.{number}" for number in sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
    ]
    if os.path.exists(path):
        members.append(path)
    return members


def _resolve_members(path):
    """Pick the member files to read, honouring a published staging file.

    A compaction publishes ``path.compact`` with a single atomic rename
    of a fully written and flushed file, so the name only ever holds a
    complete whole segment.  While it exists -- during cleanup or after a
    crash interrupted cleanup -- it alone is the segment set, and the
    record sequence it yields equals the pre-compaction one item by item.
    A crash earlier, while the merge is still being written, leaves the
    half-written private temp file instead; that never carries this name
    and so neither joins recovery nor affects reads.
    """
    staging = _staging_path(path)
    if os.path.exists(staging):
        return [staging]
    return _segment_members(path)


def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.

    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
    """
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    pending = b""
    lineno = 0
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
            if not chunk:
                break
            pending += chunk
            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
            for raw in complete:
                lineno += 1
                yield lineno, raw
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _parse_file(path, label):
    """Stream one segment or the current log through the metrics parser."""
    for lineno, raw in _iter_lines(path):
        if not raw or raw == b"\r":
            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
            continue
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
            yield parse_metrics(text)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
            ) from exc


def iter_metrics(path):
    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.

    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
    a single line may be arbitrarily long.

    When a compaction has staged its merged segment at ``path.compact``
    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.

    A torn unterminated tail at the end of any file is silently discarded;
    a segment holding only a torn tail yields nothing.  Blank empty lines
    (``\\n``) and CRLF blank lines (``\\r\\n``) are skipped.  Any other
    complete line that is not a metrics JSON object raises
    :class:`ValueError` naming the file and its 1-based line number.

    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
    content problems are reported lazily as the offending line is reached.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics JSON
            object (raised while iterating).
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")

    members = _resolve_members(path)
    if not members:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")

    def _generate():
        for member in members:
            yield from _parse_file(member, member)

    return _generate()


def recover_metrics(path):
    """Read metric records back from the rotated log set at ``path``.

    Segments are read in ascending order followed by the current log; see
    :func:`iter_metrics` for the line-level rules.  This materialises the
    records into a list, while :func:`iter_metrics` streams them.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics object.
    """
    return list(iter_metrics(path))


def _iter_raw_records(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.

    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives compaction
    untouched.
    """
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    pending = b""
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
            if not chunk:
                break
            pending += chunk
            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
            for raw in complete:
                if raw and raw != b"\r":
                    yield raw + b"\n"
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _truncate_live_log(path):
    """Shrink the current log to zero bytes without unlinking its path.

    Keeping the inode and path in place means a process that waits on the
    lock during compaction never observes -- and so never recreates -- a
    missing live log: once it takes the lock the path is still the same
    empty file.
    """
    fd = os.open(
        path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
    )
    os.close(fd)


def _finish_staged_compact(path):
    """Finish compaction cleanup when a staging file is present.

    Called with the live-log lock held, both at the end of
    :func:`compact_metrics` and by any append, rotation or compaction
    that finds a staging file left by a crashed cleanup.  The staging
    file only ever holds a whole fully landed segment, so finishing is
    pure filesystem cleanup.

    The staging file stays the sole authoritative member (see
    :func:`_resolve_members`) until the final step: old numbered
    segments are removed and the current log is emptied while reads
    still resolve to staging, and only then is staging renamed onto
    ``path.1``.  The rename is atomic, so a crash at any point leaves
    either staging alone or the finished set, and the readable record
    sequence equals the pre-compaction one item by item throughout.
    """
    staging = _staging_path(path)
    if not os.path.exists(staging):
        return
    for number in _segment_numbers(path):
        os.unlink(f"{path}.{number}")
    _truncate_live_log(path)
    os.replace(staging, f"{path}.1")


def compact_metrics(path):
    """Merge every segment and the current log into one segment.

    All records are copied into the fixed segment ``path.1`` in write
    order; the current log is left empty afterwards.  Records move byte
    for byte with their original newlines -- nothing is re-rendered,
    de-duplicated or reordered, so ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key
    order are all preserved.  Residual torn lines are not records and
    are dropped; blank lines are skipped as on read; overlong single
    lines move as-is.  A completely empty set still produces an empty
    ``path.1``.

    The merge is first written to a private temporary file and only
    renamed onto ``path.compact`` after the whole file has landed and
    been flushed, so that name always holds a complete whole segment:
    a half-written file left by a crash never joins recovery and never
    affects reads.  Once staged, recovery and streaming read only that
    segment; cleanup publishes it as ``path.1``, removes the other
    numbered segments and empties the current log.  An interrupted
    cleanup is finished transparently by the next append, rotation or
    compaction.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing the
            merged segment fails.  A failed write removes the private
            temporary file and leaves the segment set untouched.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")

    fd = _open_locked(path, create=False)
    try:
        # A previous compaction may have staged its segment and died
        # before cleanup; settle that world before merging again.
        _finish_staged_compact(path)

        staging = _staging_path(path)
        tmp = staging + ".tmp"
        try:
            out = os.open(
                tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666
            )
            try:
                for member in _segment_members(path):
                    for raw in _iter_raw_records(member):
                        view = memoryview(raw)
                        while view:
                            written = os.write(out, view)
                            view = view[written:]
                os.fsync(out)
            finally:
                os.close(out)

            # Atomic publication: from this instant the whole merged
            # segment is the only member reads may use during cleanup.
            os.rename(tmp, staging)
        except BaseException:
            # Nothing reached the staging name: the private temp is the
            # only file touched, so removing it leaves the old segments
            # and current log exactly as they were.
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            raise
        _finish_staged_compact(path)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def resume_metrics(path, position=0):
    """Stream records starting at integer read position ``position``.

    ``position`` counts records already read from the start of the
    segment set in write order, exactly the records :func:`iter_metrics`
    yields; omitting it (or passing 0) reads from the beginning.  The
    position needs no conversion across appends, rotations, compactions
    or crash-driven compaction cleanup -- it only ever counts records --
    and stays valid as long as it does not exceed the current record
    total, at which point the result is an empty stream.  Exactly like
    :func:`iter_metrics`, reading is line by line and takes time linear
    in the skipped-and-yielded prefix without materialising the segment
    set; an overrun is reported once the end is reached.

    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
    content problems and an out-of-range position are reported lazily
    while iterating.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
        TypeError: ``position`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
        ValueError: ``position`` is negative or past the record total
            (the latter raised while iterating), or a complete line is
            not a metrics JSON object.
    """
    # Eager path validation first, matching iter_metrics/recover_metrics.
    records = iter_metrics(path)
    if isinstance(position, bool) or not isinstance(position, int):
        raise TypeError(
            f"read position must be an integer, got {type(position).__name__}"
        )
    if position < 0:
        raise ValueError("read position must not be negative")

    def _generate():
        remaining = position
        for record in records:
            if remaining:
                remaining -= 1
                continue
            yield record
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                f"read position {position} exceeds the record total of "
                f"{position - remaining}"
            )

    return _generate()

def _staging_path(path):
    """The compaction staging file path (``path.compact``)."""
    return path + _COMPACT_SUFFIX


def _pruned_path(path):
    """The sidecar path remembering the cumulative pruned-record count."""
    return path + _PRUNED_SUFFIX


def _read_pruned(path):
    """Return the cumulative number of pruned records recorded on disk.

    The sidecar holds one base-ten integer written atomically by
    :func:`prune_metrics`; an absent sidecar -- every segment set that was
    never pruned, including all pre-pruning sets -- reads back as zero.
    """
    sidecar = _pruned_path(path)
    try:
        fd = os.open(sidecar, os.O_RDONLY)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 0
    try:
        data = b""
        while True:
            chunk = os.read(fd, _READ_CHUNK)
            if not chunk:
                break
            data += chunk
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    return int(data.decode("utf-8").strip())


def _write_pruned(path, count):
    """Atomically replace the pruned-record sidecar with ``count``."""
    sidecar = _pruned_path(path)
    tmp = sidecar + ".tmp"
    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666)
    try:
        payload = str(count).encode("ascii")
        view = memoryview(payload)
        while view:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
            view = view[written:]
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    os.replace(tmp, sidecar)


def _find_prune_marker(path):
    """Find a published prune marker left by an interrupted prune.

    Returns ``(kind, segment_number, count, marker_path)`` or ``None``.
    Segment number ``0`` names the current log; the sidecar and private
    temporary files never match the marker pattern.
    """
    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + _PRUNE_MARKER_SUFFIX
    try:
        names = os.listdir(directory or ".")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    matches = []
    for name in names:
        if not name.startswith(prefix):
            continue
        parts = name[len(prefix):].split(".")
        if len(parts) != 3:
            continue
        kind, number, count = parts
        if kind not in (_MARKER_TRUNCATE, _MARKER_EVICT):
            continue
        if not (number.isascii() and number.isdigit()):
            continue
        if not (count.isascii() and count.isdigit()):
            continue
        matches.append((name, kind, int(number), int(count)))
    if not matches:
        return None
    # A prune publishes exactly one marker; several names can only be a
    # leftover of an impossible state, so resolve deterministically.
    name, kind, number, count = sorted(matches)[0]
    return kind, number, count, os.path.join(directory, name) if directory else name


def _finish_prune_marker(path):
    """Finish an interrupted prune whose marker is still published.

    Called with the live-log lock held by any mutating operation, mirroring
    :func:`_finish_staged_compact`.  The marker alone names the new world
    until cleanup completes:

    * a truncate marker's own bytes are the surviving tail of the cut
      segment; lower numbered segments are removed, the new pruned count
      is persisted, and the marker is atomically renamed onto the cut
      segment (or onto the live log for segment number zero);
    * an evict marker removes every numbered segment through its number,
      persists the new count, and removes itself; the live log survives.

    The sidecar is written before the marker disappears, so a crash at any
    point leaves readers resolving either through the marker or through an
    already-updated sidecar -- never with the old count over the new files.
    """
    marker = _find_prune_marker(path)
    if marker is None:
        return
    kind, number, count, marker_path = marker
    if kind == _MARKER_TRUNCATE:
        for other in sorted(_segment_numbers(path)):
            if other < number:
                os.unlink(f"{path}.{other}")
        _write_pruned(path, count)
        target = path if number == 0 else f"{path}.{number}"
        os.replace(marker_path, target)
    else:
        for other in sorted(_segment_numbers(path)):
            if other <= number:
                os.unlink(f"{path}.{other}")
        _write_pruned(path, count)
        os.unlink(marker_path)

def prune_metrics(path, quota):
    """Stream records starting at integer read position ``position``.

    ``position`` counts records already read from the start of the
    segment set in write order, exactly the records :func:`iter_metrics`
    yields; omitting it (or passing 0) reads from the beginning.  The
    position needs no conversion across appends, rotations, compactions
    or crash-driven compaction cleanup -- it only ever counts records --
    and stays valid as long as it does not exceed the current record
    total, at which point the result is an empty stream.  Exactly like
    :func:`iter_metrics`, reading is line by line and takes time linear
    in the skipped-and-yielded prefix without materialising the segment
    set; an overrun is reported once the end is reached.

    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
    content problems and an out-of-range position are reported lazily
    while iterating.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
        TypeError: ``position`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
        ValueError: ``position`` is negative or past the record total
            (the latter raised while iterating), or a complete line is
            not a metrics JSON object.
    """
    # Eager path validation first, matching iter_metrics/recover_metrics.
    records = iter_metrics(path)
    if isinstance(position, bool) or not isinstance(position, int):
        raise TypeError(
            f"read position must be an integer, got {type(position).__name__}"
        )
    if position < 0:
        raise ValueError("read position must not be negative")

    def _generate():
        remaining = position
        for record in records:
            if remaining:
                remaining -= 1
                continue
            yield record
        if remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                f"read position {position} exceeds the record total of "
                f"{position - remaining}"
            )

    return _generate()

def prune_metrics(path, quota):
    """Stream records starting at integer read position ``position``.

    ``position`` counts records already read from the start of the
    segment set in write order, exactly the records :func:`iter_metrics`
    yields; omitting it (or passing 0) reads from the beginning.  The
    position needs no conversion across appends, rotations, compactions
    or crash-driven compaction cleanup -- it only ever counts records --
    and stays valid as long as it does not exceed the current record
    total, at which point the result is an empty stream.  Exactly like
    :func:`iter_metrics`, reading is line by line and takes time linear
    in the skipped-and-yielded prefix without materialising the segment
    set; an overrun is reported once the end is reached.

    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
    content problems and an out-of-range position are reported lazily
    while iterating.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
        TypeError: ``position`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
        ValueError: ``position`` is negative or past the record total
            (the latter raised while iterating), or a complete line is
            not a metrics JSON object.
    """

    records = iter_metrics(path)

def prune_metrics(path, quota):
    """Enforce a retention ``quota`` of records by evicting from the oldest end.

    ``quota`` is the greatest number of records the segment set keeps;
    records are dropped whole, in write order, and a record is never split
    in two.  A quota of zero evicts every record; a quota at or above the
    current record total evicts nothing.  Empty segments and segments
    holding only a torn tail consume no quota.  Only the one segment the
    cut lands inside is rewritten -- with its surviving complete records
    copied byte for byte, blank lines and torn tails dropped -- while
    every wholly evicted segment is simply deleted, so the work grows with
    the amount evicted, not with the segment set.

    Evicted records keep occupying their original write-order positions:
    the cumulative number of evicted records is remembered in a
    ``path.pruned`` sidecar and a read position is always an ordinal in
    write order.  See :func:`resume_metrics`.

    The eviction first lands in a private temporary file and is then
    published under a single marker name (``path.prune.<kind>.<n>.<c>``)
    with one atomic rename, so the name only ever names a complete
    boundary: a crash before publication leaves the segment set exactly as
    it was, and a crash afterwards leaves a fully evicted-to-boundary set
    whose cleanup the next append, rotation, compaction or prune finishes
    transparently.  An unfinished compaction is settled first.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing fails.
        TypeError: ``quota`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
        ValueError: ``quota`` is negative.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
    if isinstance(quota, bool) or not isinstance(quota, int):
        raise TypeError(
            f"retention quota must be an integer, got {type(quota).__name__}"
        )
    if quota < 0:
        raise ValueError("retention quota must not be negative")
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")

    fd = _open_locked(path, create=False)
    try:
        if fcntl is None:
            # No lock is carried on this platform; release the live-log
            # descriptor before cleanup replaces or truncates named paths
            # (Windows rejects replacing an open file).
            os.close(fd)
            fd = None
        _finish_staged_compact(path)
        _finish_prune_marker(path)

        members = _segment_members(path)
        if not members:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")
        pruned = _read_pruned(path)

        counts = [
            sum(1 for _ in _iter_raw_records(member)) for member in members
        ]
        physical_total = sum(counts)
        retained = pruned + physical_total
        if quota >= retained or physical_total == 0:
            # Nothing to evict: quota already satisfied, or no complete
            # records remain physically (blank/torn-only files).
            return
        drop = min(retained - quota, physical_total)

        boundary = 0
        cut_index = -1
        cut_within = 0
        for index, count in enumerate(counts):
            if boundary + count >= drop:
                cut_index = index
                cut_within = drop - boundary
                break
            boundary += count

        cut_member = members[cut_index]
        new_pruned = pruned + drop
        if cut_member == path:
            cut_number = 0
        else:
            cut_number = int(cut_member[len(path) + 1:])

        if cut_within == counts[cut_index]:
            # The cut lands on a segment boundary: publish an eviction
            # marker naming the oldest surviving point.  Number zero is
            # the current log, which is emptied rather than unlinked.
            kind = _MARKER_EVICT
        else:
            kind = _MARKER_TRUNCATE
        marker = (
            f"{path}{_PRUNE_MARKER_SUFFIX}{kind}.{cut_number}.{new_pruned}"
        )
        tmp = marker + ".tmp"
        out = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666)
        try:
            if kind == _MARKER_TRUNCATE:
                # Copy only the complete records that survive inside the
                # cut segment; torn tails and blank lines never move.
                record_index = 0
                for raw in _iter_raw_records(cut_member):
                    record_index += 1
                    if record_index <= cut_within:
                        continue
                    view = memoryview(raw)
                    while view:
                        written = os.write(out, view)
                        view = view[written:]
            os.fsync(out)
        finally:
            os.close(out)
        try:
            # Atomic publication: from this instant reads resolve through
            # the marker to exactly the surviving record sequence.
            os.replace(tmp, marker)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            raise
        _finish_prune_marker(path)
    finally:
        if fd is not None:
            os.close(fd)


def resume_metrics(path, position=0):
    """Stream records starting at integer read position ``position``.

    ``position`` is the record ordinal in write order, counting records
    already read from the start of the segment set -- records since pruned
    away included, since pruned records keep their original ordinals and
    the segment set remembers how many were evicted.  Omitting it (or
    passing 0) reads from the oldest surviving record.  A position inside
    the pruned prefix, or exactly at the prune boundary, likewise starts
    at the oldest surviving record.  The position needs no conversion
    across appends, rotations, compactions, pruning or crash cleanup.  It
    is only out of range when it exceeds the record total *including*
    evicted records; a position equal to the total yields an empty stream.

    Exactly like :func:`iter_metrics`, reading is line by line and takes
    time linear in the skipped-and-yielded prefix without materialising
    the segment set; an overrun is reported once the end is reached.  At
    any instant -- before or after pruning -- the result equals the
    matching slice of a fresh recovery from the start.

    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
    content problems and an out-of-range position are reported lazily
    while iterating.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
        TypeError: ``position`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
        ValueError: ``position`` is negative or past the record total
            (the latter raised while iterating), or a complete line is
            not a metrics JSON object.
    """
    # Eager path validation first, matching iter_metrics/recover_metrics.
    records = iter_metrics(path)
    if isinstance(position, bool) or not isinstance(position, int):
        raise TypeError(
            f"read position must be an integer, got {type(position).__name__}"
        )
    if position < 0:
        raise ValueError("read position must not be negative")

    def _generate():
        pruned = _effective_pruned(path)
        # Translate the write-order ordinal into a physical offset among
        # the surviving records; a position in the pruned prefix starts at
        # the oldest survivor rather than overshooting it.
        skip = max(position - pruned, 0)
        physical = 0
        for record in records:
            physical += 1
            if skip:
                skip -= 1
                continue
            yield record
        if position > pruned + physical:
            raise ValueError(
                f"read position {position} exceeds the record total of "
                f"{pruned + physical}"
            )

    return _generate()

1	"""Durable append-only metric log with rotation, compaction and resume.
2	
3	Each metric occupies exactly one newline-terminated JSON line.  A record is
4	appended with :func:`os.write` against a single ``O_APPEND`` file
5	descriptor, so concurrent appending processes never interleave one line
6	with another.  Recovery acknowledges only newline-terminated lines: a
7	record torn by a mid-write crash survives as an unterminated tail and is
8	silently discarded.
9	
10	:func:`rotate_metrics` seals the current log into a numbered segment
11	(``path.1``, ``path.2``, ...) and leaves an empty log behind.  Segment
12	numbers are one past the highest number ever used, so deleting a segment
13	from the outside never makes its number come back.  Recovery walks the
14	segments in ascending order followed by the current log, so a record
15	accepted before a rotation never crosses a segment boundary.
16	:func:`iter_metrics` performs the same walk as a line-by-line generator,
17	never loading the segment set into memory.
18	
19	:func:`compact_metrics` merges every segment and the current log into the
20	single fixed segment ``path.1`` and leaves an empty current log.  Records
21	are copied byte for byte, still newline terminated, without re-rendering.
22	The merge lands first in a staging file at ``path.compact``; only after it
23	is fully on disk does cleanup begin.
24	
25	:func:`prune_metrics` enforces a record-count retention quota by evicting
26	whole records from the oldest end.  The segment set remembers how many
27	records were evicted in a ``path.pruned`` counter sidecar, so read
28	positions -- ordinal numbers in write order -- never shift: evicted
29	records keep occupying their original positions.
30	
31	:func:`resume_metrics` resumes the same write-order walk at an integer
32	read position counting records already read from the start, evicted
33	records included; the position needs no translation across appends,
34	rotations, compactions, pruning or crash cleanup.
35	"""

65	_PRUNE_MARKER_SUFFIX = ".prune."

73	def _segment_numbers(path):
74	    """Return the already-used segment numbers for ``path`` as a set.
75	
76	    The ``path.compact`` staging file is never a numbered segment and is
77	    deliberately invisible here.
78	    """
79	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
80	    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + "."
81	    numbers = set()
82	    try:
83	        names = os.listdir(directory or ".")
84	    except FileNotFoundError:
85	        return numbers

87	        if name.startswith(prefix):
88	            suffix = name[len(prefix):]

106	def _read_pruned(path):
107	    """Return the cumulative number of pruned records recorded on disk.
108	
109	    The sidecar holds one base-ten integer written atomically by
110	    :func:`prune_metrics`; an absent sidecar -- every segment set that was
111	    never pruned, including all pre-pruning sets -- reads back as zero.
112	    """
113	    sidecar = _pruned_path(path)
114	    try:
115	        fd = os.open(sidecar, os.O_RDONLY)
116	    except FileNotFoundError:
117	        return 0
118	    try:
119	        data = b""
120	        while True:
121	            chunk = os.read(fd, _READ_CHUNK)
122	            if not chunk:
123	                break
124	            data += chunk
125	    finally:
126	        os.close(fd)

130	def _write_pruned(path, count):
131	    """Atomically replace the pruned-record sidecar with ``count``."""
132	    sidecar = _pruned_path(path)
133	    tmp = sidecar + ".tmp"
134	    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666)
135	    try:
136	        payload = str(count).encode("ascii")
137	        view = memoryview(payload)
138	        while view:
139	            written = os.write(fd, view)
140	            view = view[written:]
141	        os.fsync(fd)
142	    finally:
143	        os.close(fd)
144	    os.replace(tmp, sidecar)

147	def _find_prune_marker(path):
148	    """Find a published prune marker left by an interrupted prune.
149	
150	    Returns ``(kind, segment_number, count, marker_path)`` or ``None``.
151	    Segment number ``0`` names the current log; the sidecar and private
152	    temporary files never match the marker pattern.
153	    """
154	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
155	    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + _PRUNE_MARKER_SUFFIX
156	    try:
157	        names = os.listdir(directory or ".")
158	    except FileNotFoundError:
159	        return None
160	    matches = []
161	    for name in names:
162	        if not name.startswith(prefix):
163	            continue
164	        parts = name[len(prefix):].split(".")
165	        if len(parts) != 3:
166	            continue
167	        kind, number, count = parts
168	        if kind not in (_MARKER_TRUNCATE, _MARKER_EVICT):
169	            continue
170	        if not (number.isascii() and number.isdigit()):
171	            continue
172	        if not (count.isascii() and count.isdigit()):
173	            continue
174	        matches.append((name, kind, int(number), int(count)))
175	    if not matches:
176	        return None
177	    # A prune publishes exactly one marker; several names can only be a
178	    # leftover of an impossible state, so resolve deterministically.
179	    name, kind, number, count = sorted(matches)[0]
180	    return kind, number, count, os.path.join(directory, name) if directory else name

183	def _finish_prune_marker(path):
184	    """Finish an interrupted prune whose marker is still published.
185	
186	    Called with the live-log lock held by any mutating operation, mirroring
187	    :func:`_finish_staged_compact`.  The marker alone names the new world
188	    until cleanup completes:
189	
190	    * a truncate marker's own bytes are the surviving tail of the cut
191	      segment; lower numbered segments are removed, the new pruned count
192	      is persisted, and the marker is atomically renamed onto the cut
193	      segment (or onto the live log for segment number zero);
194	    * an evict marker removes every numbered segment through its number,
195	      persists the new count, and removes itself; the live log survives.
196	
197	    The sidecar is written before the marker disappears, so a crash at any
198	    point leaves readers resolving either through the marker or through an
199	    already-updated sidecar -- never with the old count over the new files.
200	    """
201	    marker = _find_prune_marker(path)
202	    if marker is None:
203	        return
204	    kind, number, count, marker_path = marker
205	    if kind == _MARKER_TRUNCATE:
206	        for other in sorted(_segment_numbers(path)):
207	            if number == 0 or other < number:

221	            _truncate_live_log(path)

226	def _same_inode(fd, path):
227	    """True when ``fd`` still names the file currently found at ``path``.
228	
229	    A rotation can rename the file while we wait for its lock, leaving the
230	    descriptor aimed at a sealed segment.  A momentarily missing ``path``
231	    (rotation crashed before recreating it) also reports False, so an
232	    appender reopens and recreates the live log.
233	    """
234	    try:
235	        current = os.stat(path)
236	    except FileNotFoundError:
237	        return False
238	    held = os.fstat(fd)
239	    return (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == (held.st_dev, held.st_ino)

242	def _open_locked(path, create):
243	    """Open the current log, take the exclusive lock, and follow rotation.
244	
245	    Waits for the inter-process lock and then re-checks that the
246	    descriptor still names the live inode: a rotation may have swapped the
247	    path to a fresh file while we waited.  When that happened the sealed
248	    descriptor is dropped and the call re-opens the new current log and
249	    takes its lock, so a record is never written into a segment and two
250	    rotations never pick the same segment number.
251	
252	    ``create`` determines whether a missing log is created (append) or
253	    reported (rotation).  A lock failure closes the descriptor and leaves
254	    nothing written.
255	    """
256	    def _open():
257	        if create:
258	            return os.open(
259	                path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
260	            )
261	        return os.open(path, os.O_RDWR)
262	
263	    fd = _open()
264	    if fcntl is None:
265	        return fd
266	    try:
267	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
268	    except OSError:
269	        os.close(fd)
270	        raise
271	    while not _same_inode(fd, path):
272	        os.close(fd)
273	        fd = _open()
274	        try:
275	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
276	        except OSError:
277	            os.close(fd)
278	            raise
279	    return fd

283	    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.
284	
285	    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
286	    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
287	    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number

291	    in the current log, never split across two.

294	    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the

305	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")

458	            # cleanup has emptied it; its old bytes are still evicted.
459	            members.append(path)
460	        return members
461	    return _segment_members(path)
462

464	def _physical_record_count(path):
465	    """Count complete surviving records across the resolved member files."""
466	    total = 0
467	    for member in _resolve_members(path):
468	        for _ in _iter_raw_records(member):
469	            total += 1
470	    return total

473	def _effective_pruned(path):
474	    """Cumulative pruned count honoring an unpublished prune marker.
475	
476	    The sidecar only reaches its new value during marker cleanup, so while
477	    a marker is published its own carried count is authoritative.
478	    """
479	    marker = _find_prune_marker(path)
480	    if marker is not None:
481	        return marker[2]

485	def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
486	    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.
487	
488	    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
489	    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
490	    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
491	    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
492	    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
493	    """
494	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
495	    pending = b""
496	    lineno = 0
497	    try:
498	        while True:
499	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
500	            if not chunk:
501	                break
502	            pending += chunk
503	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
504	            for raw in complete:
505	                lineno += 1
506	                yield lineno, raw
507	    finally:
508	        os.close(fd)

511	def _parse_file(path, label):
512	    """Stream one segment or the current log through the metrics parser."""
513	    for lineno, raw in _iter_lines(path):
514	        if not raw or raw == b"\r":
515	            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
516	            continue
517	        try:
518	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
519	            yield parse_metrics(text)
520	        except ValueError as exc:
521	            raise ValueError(
522	                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
523	            ) from exc

526	def iter_metrics(path):
527	    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.
528	
529	    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
530	    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
531	    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
532	    a single line may be arbitrarily long.
533	
534	    When a compaction has staged its merged segment at ``path.compact``
535	    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
536	    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
537	    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.
538	
539	    A torn unterminated tail at the end of any file is silently discarded;
540	    a segment holding only a torn tail yields nothing.  Blank empty lines
541	    (``\\n``) and CRLF blank lines (``\\r\\n``) are skipped.  Any other
542	    complete line that is not a metrics JSON object raises
543	    :class:`ValueError` naming the file and its 1-based line number.
544	
545	    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
546	    content problems are reported lazily as the offending line is reached.
547	
548	    Raises:
549	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
550	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
551	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
552	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics JSON
553	            object (raised while iterating).
554	    """
555	    if not isinstance(path, str):
556	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
557	    if os.path.isdir(path):
558	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
559	
560	    members = _resolve_members(path)
561	    if not members:
562	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")
563	
564	    def _generate():
565	        for member in members:
566	            yield from _parse_file(member, member)
567	
568	    return _generate()

571	def recover_metrics(path):
572	    """Read metric records back from the rotated log set at ``path``.
573	
574	    Segments are read in ascending order followed by the current log; see
575	    :func:`iter_metrics` for the line-level rules.  This materialises the
576	    records into a list, while :func:`iter_metrics` streams them.
577	
578	    Raises:
579	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
580	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
581	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics object.
582	    """
583	    return list(iter_metrics(path))
584

586	def _iter_raw_records(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
587	    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.
588	
589	    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
590	    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
591	    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
592	    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
593	    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives compaction
594	    untouched.
595	    """
596	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
597	    pending = b""
598	    try:
599	        while True:
600	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
601	            if not chunk:
602	                break
603	            pending += chunk
604	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
605	            for raw in complete:
606	                if raw and raw != b"\r":
607	                    yield raw + b"\n"
608	    finally:
609	        os.close(fd)
610	
611	
612	def _truncate_live_log(path):
613	    """Shrink the current log to zero bytes without unlinking its path.
614	
615	    Keeping the inode and path in place means a process that waits on the
616	    lock during compaction never observes -- and so never recreates -- a
617	    missing live log: once it takes the lock the path is still the same
618	    empty file.
619	    """
620	    fd = os.open(
621	        path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
622	    )
623	    os.close(fd)
624
